subject: Novacorp vendor fit & migration trigger plan
messages:
From: Elena Campos <elena@novacorp.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@novacorp.com>
Date: 2026-08-26T09:12:00Z
Subject: Request: vendor comparison + price-match ask

Karthik —

Thanks for taking a look last week. We did a quick side-by-side between our incumbent (CloudForge) and Redwood’s hosted + dedicated options. The economics look promising but procurement needs two things before we can move to a commercial review: a) a concise interoperability/ops scorecard so we can validate migration lift, and b) a one-page price-match proposal that maps to the line items in the attached econ sheet.

Key constraints:
- Migration window no longer than 60 days once SOW signed.
- Need SOC2 + data retention policy confirmation for EU data (we are hybrid).
- Prefer an annual commit option but open to a 12-month ramp if the initial commit is matched.

Attached: novacorp-econ-sheet.xlsx (cost buckets + current committed rates).

Can you send an internal scorecard and a proposed matched package by EOD Thursday?

Best,
Elena
Director, Cloud Platforms
Novacorp

---

(Attachment: novacorp-econ-sheet.xlsx - budget worksheet, 1 sheet)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: jonas_weber <jonas@redwoodinference.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>, stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwoodinference.com>, rishi_malhotra <rishi@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-26T12:05:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Request: vendor comparison + price-match ask — suggested approach

Team — forwarding Novacorp’s ask. Quick plan below; I’ll own the customer-facing delivery.

1) Interop/operational scorecard (matrix: model compatibility, KV cache portability, inference latency delta, data egress impact, onboarding effort). Deliverable: single CSV + one-page summary. (See interop-scorecard-draft.csv).
2) Commercial proposal: price-match baseline (tokens/embedding/unit) + 6 months migration support credits (technical onboarding hours + dedicated SRE during cutover).
3) Compliance evidence: SOC2 snapshot, EU data handling note + point-of-contact for Private deployment.
4) Legal redlines: prepare a slim redline term sheet that preserves our liability and includes rollback fallback.

Constraints: keep concessions minimal — prefer credits over permanent discount. If procurement pushes for deeper discount, we can trade for a 12-month committed volume.

Deliverables & owners:
- Scorecard draft: Jonas (today EOD) — interop-scorecard-draft.csv
- Concession framework: Laura + Rishi (tomorrow morning) — concession-framework.md
- Customer-facing price-match + term-sheet: me (Thu EOD) — I will include HubSpot link/next steps.

Attaching initial draft scorecard. Comments inline please.

Thanks,
Karthik
VP, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

(Attachment: interop-scorecard-draft.csv - draft matrix with initial scoring)

From: jonas_weber <jonas@redwoodinference.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-27T08:20:00Z
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request: vendor comparison + price-match ask — scorecard notes

Karthik —

I reviewed the draft scorecard and adjusted the weights to emphasize runtime compatibility and go-live risk. High-level findings:

- Functional parity: 8/10 (we support the model families they use, minor tokenization differences).
- KV cache portability: 6/10 (requires small adapter for session IDs; low dev effort).
- Latency under their sequence distributions: Redwood median +12% vs incumbent on current smallest instance; we can close this with autoscale + batching tweaks during ramp.
- Egress cost: our embeddings unit pricing is neutral after applying the suggested credits.
- Operational lift: onboarding estimate is 4–6 engineer-weeks including validation harness and test prompts.

Recommendation:
- Offer a targeted migration credit (equivalent to 2 months of committed spend) and a 90-day runbook-backed SLA during the cutover window.
- Keep list-price intact; map the credit as an implementation support credit (non-recurring).
- If they ask for steep list discount (>15%), ask for 12-month committed volume and accelerated payment.

I’ve attached a short concession framework that outlines trade-offs and approvals required.

—Jonas
Principal Solutions Architect

(Attachment: concession-framework.md - proposed approval ladder and trade-off table)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Campos <elena@novacorp.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@novacorp.com>, laura_bennett <laura@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-08-28T16:40:00Z
Subject: Novacorp vendor fit & proposed migration package

Elena —

Thanks for the clear ask. We went through the scorecard and internal approvals and here’s a concise package for Novacorp: 

1) Price match: Redwood will match incumbent list rates for token generation and embedding units for the first 12 months, subject to a 12-month minimal commit (details mapped in the attached redline-term-sheet.pdf).
2) Migration support credit: one-time implementation credit equal to two months of expected committed spend (applied as account credit).
3) Cutover support: dedicated SRE + 90-day operational runbook and canary plan during migration window.
4) Compliance: SOC2 snapshot attached; we will provide EU data handling note and customer-specific architecture diagram within 48 hours.

We prefer to structure the economic concession as a one-time credit and not a permanent list-price reduction. If Novacorp needs a permanent discount we would require an increase in committed volume.

Links and attachments: HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example/deal/NOV-2026-337; Redlined terms: redline-term-sheet.pdf; SOC2 evidence link included in Drive (shared).

Next steps:
- If this aligns, I’ll send a mutual action plan and a DocuSign-ready term sheet for legal review.
- Please confirm any additional procurement constraints (e.g., PO terms, audit windows).

Best,
Karthik
VP, Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference

(Attachment: redline-term-sheet.pdf - 3 pages, proposed commercial redlines)

From: Elena Campos <elena@novacorp.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@novacorp.com>
Date: 2026-08-30T09:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Novacorp vendor fit & proposed migration package

Karthik —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. High level: this looks reasonable. Procurement asked for two small clarifications before we engage legal:

1) Can the migration credit be defined in the SOW as an implementation credit rather than an invoice-level rebate? They prefer credits tied to deliverables.
2) We need confirmation that the 12-month commit level is measured on billed tokens (not list units) to align forecasting.

If you can confirm those two items I’ll route the redline to legal and sign the MOP (mutual action plan) link you provide. We’d like to target the migration window to start by 2026-10-01 if possible.

Thanks — I’ll await the quick clarifications.

Best,
Elena
Director, Cloud Platforms
Novacorp
